chapterName: Empire: From Constantine's Sons to Theodosius (AD 337-395)

questions.question: What gave Theodosius victory at the river Frigidus in 394?
options: A fierce wind in the enemy's faces
A flood sweeping away the enemy camp
questions.explanation: A fierce wind blew into the enemy's faces and decided the battle, fought in today's Slovenia. The win left Theodosius ruler of the whole empire.
questions.sourceQuote: In September 394, at the river Frigidus in today's Slovenia, a fierce wind blew into the enemy's faces and gave Theodosius victory.

questions.question: What became of Julian's half-brother after Constantius II made him deputy in the east?
options: He was killed by his own troops
He usurped power in the west
He ruled by terror and was executed
questions.explanation: The young man ruled by terror and was executed in 354. That left Julian the last male of his line, and he was held under suspicion at Milan.
questions.sourceQuote: The young man ruled by terror and was executed in 354.

questions.question: According to most historians, why did Julian back rebuilding the Jewish Temple in Jerusalem?
options: To win Jewish support against Persia
To create a shrine to Helios
To raise new taxes in Judaea
questions.explanation: Most historians think Julian wanted to disprove a Christian prophecy. The work stopped after fires, perhaps caused by an earthquake.
questions.sourceQuote: He also backed rebuilding the Jewish Temple in Jerusalem, most historians think to disprove a Christian prophecy.

questions.question: Which city, seized by troops loyal to Constantius, threatened to cut off Julian's march east in 361?
questions.explanation: Loyalists seized Aquileia, at the head of the Adriatic, nearly wrecking Julian's gamble. He was left waiting in the Balkans until Constantius died.
questions.sourceQuote: The gamble nearly failed when troops loyal to Constantius seized Aquileia, a city at the head of the Adriatic, threatening to cut him off.

questions.question: According to the most trusted account, what sparked the riot in Thessalonica in 390?
options: A bishop was arrested for heresy
A general jailed a popular charioteer
questions.explanation: The crowd demanded the charioteer's release, and when the general refused, the mob killed him. Soldiers later took a bloody revenge.
questions.sourceQuote: According to the most trusted account, a general had jailed a popular charioteer, and the crowd demanded his release.

questions.question: How do modern scholars regard the story of Ambrose physically barring the cathedral door against Theodosius?
questions.explanation: Modern scholars call the famous door-barring scene a pious fiction. In reality Ambrose wrote to the emperor refusing him communion until he did penance.
questions.sourceQuote: Modern scholars call this a pious fiction.

questions.question: Why did Valens not wait for the western emperor before fighting at Adrianople?
options: He wanted a victory of his own
The western army had turned back
The Goths were about to escape
questions.explanation: The young western emperor asked Valens to wait, but Valens wanted the glory for himself. His tired, thirsty troops then marched about 12 km in summer heat.
questions.sourceQuote: The young western emperor, Gratian, was marching to help and asked him to wait, but Valens wanted a victory of his own.

questions.question: Which of these were among Julian's government reforms? (select all that apply)
options: Handing power back to city councils
Doubling the size of the palace staff
questions.explanation: Julian returned power to the city councils (curiae) and cancelled unpaid land taxes. He also dismissed thousands of palace servants and joined Senate debates as an ordinary member.
questions.sourceQuote: He handed power back to the city councils (*curiae*) and cancelled unpaid land taxes.

questions.question: What order from Constantius II in February 360 set off the mutiny of Julian's troops?
options: To send over half the army east
questions.explanation: Constantius ordered more than half of Julian's army to march east against Persia, bypassing Julian himself. The soldiers did not want to leave Gaul and proclaimed Julian Augustus.
questions.sourceQuote: In February 360, Constantius II ordered more than half of Julian's army in Gaul to march east.

questions.question: Which confederation of tribes from the upper Rhine attacked Julian at Strasbourg?
questions.explanation: The Alamanni attacked a heavily outnumbered Roman army and were routed. Their king was captured and many were driven into the river.
questions.sourceQuote: An army of the Alamanni, a confederation of tribes from the upper Rhine, attacked him.
